body.x: Newjak Co., Ltd. was named a 2027 Honoree in Artificial Intelligence at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards.
The winning product is SPACEON, an Autonomous Spatial Intelligence Platform.

Traditional spatial experiences require people to adapt to content. SPACEON reverses that relationship. SPACEON is an AI-powered Autonomous Spatial Intelligence Platform that turns physical spaces into adaptive, intelligent environments with no headsets, wearables or controllers.

Through LiDAR-based full-body sensing and AI perception models, the platform understands users and spatial context in real time. Based on this understanding, SPACEON continuously adapts content, difficulty, roles and interactions throughout each experience.

Instead of delivering the same scenario to every visitor, SPACEON creates personalized experiences that evolve with each individual's behavior, and it coordinates groups of users simultaneously within a single shared space.
SPACEON is designed for entertainment, education, exhibitions and retail. It operates as a unified AI platform that runs multiple applications on the same physical infrastructure.

AVING News, a global media outlet that has covered the CES floor for 21 years, runs the 'AVING CES Newsroom (avingces.news)' special page to spread innovation news more effectively in the AI era. Through more than 1,000 reports and hundreds of on-site video interviews every year, AVING NEWS has supported the global scale-up of Korean startups. At CES 2027 as well, it will set up the 'AVING TECH TALK' broadcast zone at the Venetian Expo (Hall A, Booth 50271) and vividly deliver news of Korean innovative companies to the world.

AVING News will also hold the '3rd Innovation Awards Winners Networking Party' at 5 p.m. on Wednesday, Nov. 25, at MIK BASE CAMP, and will conduct separate video interviews with participating companies (registration: Eventus). In early December, it plans to launch pre-coverage in earnest, including a foreign media interview program with U.S. media outlets that cover CES every year and serve as Innovation Awards judging media.
* AVING News uses AI tools when editing articles.
